newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks down 2.10 pct on economic concerns.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks down 2.10 pct on economic concerns.

text.p: Thai stocks lost 2.10 percent at 0753 GMT on Wednesday on selling linked to concerns about the Thai economic outlook and an arson at Sanyo Universal's warehouse and offices that analysts feared could scare away investors.

"I think foreigners are doing the major selling. When the Bank of Thailand defends the baht, they don't think this is normal as the value of most currencies goes with economic performance," said a trader at Phatra Thanakit.
Thailand's growing current account deficit and slowing economic growth have put pressure on the baht early this week, promptimg the central bank to intervene in the Singapore market.
"It may take some time for confidence to return," he said.

Brokers said the market is expected to face further short term setbacks after an overnight arson at Sanyo Electric's Thai warehouse and office complex which, they said, could damage Thailand's investment climate.
Krung Thai Bank topped the active list on reports that employees may choose to strike to protest against smaller bonuses offered by the management after its increased loan loss provisions this year.
The bank was down three baht to 56.50 in mid afternoon on Wednesday. -- James Mclean (662) 652 0642
